page: Microsoft Azure FX2ms_v2 is a compute-focused yet memory-dense instance hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, the instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core via hyperthreading. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features modern instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and advanced cryptographic extensions like AES-NI and SHA-NI. The instance allocates an unusually high memory footprint for its core count, delivering 42.0 GB of RAM (21.0 GB per vCPU). It includes no local storage or bundled GPUs, requiring reliance on remote managed storage for disk volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-core processing capabilities contrasted with limited multi-threaded throughput due to the single physical core constraint. The instance reaches a Geekbench single-core score of 2335.0, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances, along with top-quartile performance in single-threaded gzip compression (34.91 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.19 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate parallel execution scales lower, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2876.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 2215.99 ranking in the lower tiers. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 21.0 GB/sec read and 14.33 GB/sec write for large uncached blocks.

In terms of workload fit, the FX2ms_v2 offers high memory-per-core density paired with high clock frequency, making it suitable for memory-intensive tasks with low thread parallelization demands. Ideal deployments include medium-scale in-memory caches, single-threaded processing pipelines, and light database or text processing tasks that benefit from significant RAM without requiring broad parallel scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure FX2ms_v2 is an x86_64 server instance optimized for workloads requiring high single-core performance alongside substantial memory capacity. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, it provides 2 vCPUs on 1 physical core coupled with 42.0 GB of RAM (21.0 GB per core). It has no integrated local storage or GPUs. Benchmark profiles reveal leading single-thread execution, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2335.0 and strong compression throughput, though multi-core benchmarks remain constrained by the low core count. The high 21:1 memory-to-core ratio and advanced instruction sets like AMX and AVX-512 make the instance well matched for memory-heavy single-threaded applications, in-memory caching, and specialized analytics.
